assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Uno Minda Ltd (consolidated, Rs crore). FY26 is the last reported year (revenue Rs19,658 cr incl. Rs69 cr of prior-period income). One reported segment, so revenue is a single growth path computed from the six-division build in `build` and checked in tools/authoring/UNOMINDA.ctx.js. Net profit is on the owners' basis (UNOMINDA.patch.js); the engine has no line for the share of JV profit (post-tax) or minorities, so both enter `otherIncome` grossed up for tax (see _otherIncomeWhy). Valued on P/E, as the street does; the multiple is derived in UNOMINDA.ctx.js and written here by UNOMINDA.val.js.
assumptions._revenueWhy: From the division build. FY27E +19.2% on reported FY26 (+19.6% on the Rs19,589 cr ex prior-period income): Q1FY27 grew 26% (normalised) with industry production +22%; from Q3 the base includes the GST 2.0 boost (Sep-2025), so we assume growth slows through the year. Switches +15%, Lighting +12%, Castings +22% (Kharkhoda 4W wheels, Bawal 2W wheels, aluminium pass-through), Green Mobility +60% (Q1 +78%: EV systems, 4W EDU supplies, CNG), Seating +20%, Others +17% (sensors/ADAS, sunroof from end-FY27). FY28E +17.9% and FY29E +16.9%: production +5-7% plus content, new plants (CSN wheels and EV powertrain Q2FY28, 4W seating Q4FY28) and orders already won (2W lamps Rs450 cr peak, seating exports Rs390 cr, sunroof >Rs500 cr). Street FY27E/FY28E revenue: Rs23,438-23,922 cr / Rs27,253-28,344 cr.
assumptions._marginWhy: Guidance 11% +/-50bp for FY27 'with a bias towards the higher end' (4-Aug-2026). Q1FY27 10.3% (commodity and wage inflation, ~40bp dilution from at-cost pass-through); FY26 11.1% normalised (11.5% reported incl. the prior-period income); 10.7-12.3% since FY17. FY27E 11.1% assumes ~11.3% for Q2-Q4 as price resets catch up; FY28E 11.4% and FY29E 11.5% as new plants pass their start-up year, partly offset by lower-margin EV and electronics. Street: ICICI Direct 11.1%/11.5%, Emkay 10.8%/11.5%/11.6%.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27E Rs1,750 cr guided (~Rs650 cr sustaining, ~Rs1,100 cr growth, balance land; reiterated 4-Aug-2026). Announced projects Rs3,788 cr, Rs1,406 cr spent by Jun-2026, ~Rs2,000 cr more over 18-24 months. FY26 cash capex Rs1,572 cr. FY28E Rs1,600 cr, FY29E Rs1,500 cr (sustaining ~Rs700 cr plus the tail of announced projects).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A Rs704 cr = 8.2% of average gross block (Rs8,566 cr). Part of capex is land (not depreciated) and the engine depreciates new capex at once while CWIP stays flat, so 7.8%: FY27E ~Rs800 cr (Q1FY27 Rs177 cr; Q4FY26 Rs192 cr; casting is on WDV, so Q1 is seasonally low), FY28E ~Rs930 cr, FY29E ~Rs1,050 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net debt company: Rs2,179 cr at Mar-2026 (borrowings Rs2,537 cr less cash and bank Rs358 cr; leases Rs203 cr more). Interest income is tiny (deposits Rs8 cr in FY26) and is in the recurring other income below.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built, not plugged: (1) recurring other income Rs28 / 30 / 32 cr (FY26 Rs34 cr incl. Rs5 cr tax-refund interest and Rs6 cr write-backs; Q1FY27 Rs6 cr); (2) share of JV and associate profit, post-tax, Rs270 / 310 / 350 cr (FY26 Rs249 cr, +38%; Q1FY27 Rs48 cr, flat, hit by commodity costs that the company expects to recover from Q2; Toyoda Gosei airbag plant from Q1FY27; Denso Ten IVI order Rs600 cr peak from Q3FY29) less (3) minorities Rs97 / 110 / 124 cr (FY26 Rs87 cr, Q1FY27 Rs20 cr; mostly Tokai Rika's 49% of Uno Mindarika). (2) and (3) are after tax, so they are divided by (1 - 24.5%) because the engine taxes all other income: 28 + (270 - 97) / 0.755 = Rs257 cr. Net profit then equals owners' PAT. FY26 on Screener's basis: other income Rs34 cr + JV Rs249 cr - exceptional Rs28 cr = Rs256 cr; TTM to Jun-26 Rs250 cr.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs187 cr, Q1FY27 Rs46 cr. Gross debt Rs2,537 cr plus leases Rs203 cr at Mar-2026; FY27 capex above operating cash flow keeps debt rising (MOSL/Emkay see net debt peaking in FY27), easing in FY29E.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 24.3% and Q1FY27 24.5% of profit before JV share; the new-regime rate is 25.2% with some incentive income.
assumptions._payoutWhy: 12-14% of PAT every year FY22-FY26 (FY26 Rs2.65 a share = 12.8%).

dcf._betaWhy: Cyclical auto supplier with modest leverage (net debt ~0.3x equity, ~1x EBITDA): beta 1.0, cost of equity 12.5%. Debt is ~4% of enterprise value, so we use the cost of equity as the discount rate (the engine's DCF has no separate WACC in Excel).
dcf._tgWhy: India's nominal GDP grows ~10%; vehicle production ~5-6% a year plus content per vehicle. House range 5-6%: 6%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~17% to 8% over 15 years as new categories mature.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin held at 11.5%: the company's long-run band (10.7-12.3%) with no pricing power to go higher.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~4.6% of revenue in FY29E to 4.5% (FY22-26 average 7.7% in a heavy build phase; ~4% sustaining plus growth); depreciation 3.5% of revenue (FY26 3.6%).
dcf._jvWhy: FCFF excludes JV profit (cash comes as dividends: Rs137 cr in FY26) and includes minorities' share; JVs enter only at book value (Rs924 cr) through investments in net debt. See the DCF chapter for the effect.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Industry volumes keep growing high single digits after the GST step; EV powertrain, sunroof, PV seating and exports ramp on time; alloy-wheel penetration rises again; margin reaches the top of the 11-12% band as commodity costs ease.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Volumes flatten against the GST base; commodity and wage inflation is recovered late; new plants ramp slowly (Inovance JV blocked by Chinese approvals); share losses at a key 4W client continue; margin slips back to ~10.5%.

cover.headline: A proven compounder at a fair price: the multiple, not the business, caps the upside
cover.lead: Uno Minda is India's largest maker of automotive switches and horns, a top-three lighting maker and a fast-growing supplier of alloy wheels, seats, sensors and EV parts, with Japanese-partnered JVs in airbags, filters and infotainment. Revenue grew 25% a year over FY21-26 at a steady ~11% EBITDA margin, and Q1FY27 revenue rose 26% (normalised). We forecast owners' EPS of ₹24.3 / ₹30.0 / ₹36.4 for FY27-29E, a little below the street. The street values Uno Minda on **P/E on one-year-forward EPS** (MOSL 45x FY28E). The house rule (its own forward P/E median since 2021, 38.8x, cut by the 8.4% auto-component de-rating) gives **35.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹33.2 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹970, DCF ₹589. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The growth engine is real and broad
arguments.p: Revenue grew ~23% a year over FY16-26 against 4-5% a year for car and two-wheeler production (Jefferies, Mar-2026), by adding products per vehicle and customers. Q1FY27: switches +20%, lighting +14%, castings +32%, seating +28%, Green Mobility +78% (EV systems, 4W electric drive units, CNG). FY27 brings seven new or expanded plants, the first EV-powertrain and sunroof lines, and a PV seating plant for FY28. We model revenue +{{F.salesGrowth.0|pct0}} / +{{F.salesGrowth.1|pct0}} / +{{F.salesGrowth.2|pct0}}.

arguments.h: But it is a tier-1 supplier with tier-1 margins
arguments.p: The EBITDA margin has stayed in a 10.6-12.3% band for ten years; Q1FY27 was 10.3% as commodity and wage inflation (Haryana minimum wages +~35%) were recovered late and at cost. Management guides 11% ±50bp. Capex runs at ~8% of revenue, so free cash flow is thin (₹204 cr in FY26) and net debt rises in FY27.

arguments.h: A fifth of profit comes from JVs it does not control
arguments.p: Toyoda Gosei (airbags), Roki (filters), Denso Ten (infotainment) and Tokai Rika (seatbelts) earned Uno Minda ₹249 cr in FY26 (21% of owners' profit), and ~7% of consolidated profit goes to minority partners (mainly Tokai Rika's 49% of Uno Mindarika). The JV income is in EPS but not in EBITDA, which flatters P/E-based comparisons with peers and is invisible to a DCF of consolidated cash flows.

At ₹1,170 the stock trades at 38.9x FY28E and 35.2x Sep-28E EPS, close to its own forward median since 2021 (38.8x) and below its two-year median (44.7x); auto-component stocks sat 8.4% below their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026. The street's 39-46x multiples need ~23% EPS growth for years; at 45x our target would be ~₹1,490. We like the business; the price already pays for most of it.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): whether margins recover towards 11% as commodity and wage costs are passed on, and the first quarter against the GST-boosted base from Q3.
Commissioning of the Khed EV-powertrain plant and the Bawal 2W alloy-wheel lines (H2FY27), the Farrukhnagar 4W switch plant (Q3FY27) and sunroof (Q4FY27).
China's decision on the Inovance EV-powertrain JV (Indian Press Note 3 approval received; Chinese approval pending under tighter technology-export rules).
Festive-season production (Oct-Dec 2026) and Maruti Suzuki volumes: Uno Minda lagged its key 4W client by ~12% in Q1 (Emkay).
New orders: PV seating customers beyond the anchor, sunroof (order book >₹500 cr), exports (target >₹1,500 cr from ~₹600 cr).

sections.title: A supermarket of auto parts: 28 product lines, two-wheelers and cars in equal measure

blocks.p: Uno Minda (formerly Minda Industries) is a Gurugram-based, promoter-run tier-1 supplier controlled by the Minda family (68.4%). It makes ~28 product lines in 78 plants and sells 94% to vehicle makers and 6% to the aftermarket; 89% of Q1FY27 revenue was billed in India. By vehicle, Q1FY27 revenue was 45% cars and utility vehicles, 45% two-wheelers, 4% commercial vehicles, 3% three-wheelers and 3% off-road. It reports one segment, but discloses revenue by division. Two customers were each above 10% of FY26 revenue. Around the consolidated business sit equity-accounted JVs with Japanese partners (airbags and steering wheels with Toyoda Gosei, filters with Roki, infotainment with Denso Ten, seatbelts and locks with Tokai Rika) whose combined FY26 revenue was ~₹5,660 cr; including them, "group" revenue was ₹25,203 cr.

sections.title: Sixty-eight years of adding products: horns to EV drives, built by JVs, licences and buy-outs

blocks.p: The company began in 1958 making ammeters, added horns, switches and lighting, and since the 1990s has grown by pairing with Japanese and European specialists: a licence or JV first, then, often, buying the partner out. Kosei (alloy wheels) went from JV to full merger in 2024-26; Westport (CNG) from 50% to 76%; FRIWO's 49.9% of Uno Minda EV Systems was bought in FY26 (₹141 cr plus ₹58 cr for e-drive assets). Each step moved profit from "share of JV" or "minorities" into owners' profit, which helped EPS grow faster than revenue. Equity has been issued only for ESOPs and small share-swap deals since the FY23 1:1 bonus (Screener EPS is bonus-adjusted).

sections.title: Record vehicle production in FY26 (+12%) and Q1FY27 (+22%); input costs are the catch

blocks.p: India produced ~34.7 mn vehicles in FY26 (+12%): 5.5 mn passenger vehicles (+9%), 26.6 mn two-wheelers (+12%) and 1.17 mn commercial vehicles (+13%), with a strong second half after the Sep-2025 GST cuts. Q1FY27 production was a record 9.69 mn (+22%): PVs +17%, two-wheelers +23% (exports +37%), CVs +15%. From Q3FY27 the comparison base includes the GST boost, and management itself expects a move "towards more stable technology-led growth".

sections.title: Switches and lighting: 47% of revenue, steady mid-teens growth, the core of the franchise

blocks.p: **Switches** (₹4,871 cr in FY26, +15.9%) is the largest division. In two-wheelers Uno Minda is the leading handlebar-switch supplier, growing with domestic volumes, share gains at "under-penetrated" customers and exports (2W switch exports crossed ₹280 cr in FY26; ₹95 cr in Q1FY27). In cars it sells through Uno Mindarika (51%; Tokai Rika 49%), which grew 24% to ₹525 cr in Q1FY27 and is moving from Manesar to a larger plant at Farrukhnagar (₹116 cr, Q3FY27) because it is capacity-constrained. **Lighting** (₹4,402 cr, +14%) is led by two-wheelers, where Uno Minda supplies most electric-scooter makers and won a ~₹450 cr peak-value order for unserved models (SOP H2FY28, ~25% of current 2W lighting revenue). Four-wheeler lighting tripled in five years and is now "in consolidation"; a new global OEM nominated it in Q1FY27 and ambient lighting is gaining orders. Lighting grew only 14% in Q1FY27, the slowest division.

sections.title: Castings: the capital-hungry growth engine; alloy-wheel capacity nearly doubles

blocks.p: Castings earned ₹3,694 cr in FY26 (+15%): 4W alloy wheels ₹1,964 cr, 2W alloy wheels ₹1,058 cr and aluminium die casting ₹673 cr. FY26 was held back by lower alloy-wheel penetration (fast-growing entry cars use steel wheels; some 2W programmes switched to steel); growth came from new capacity and aluminium prices (pass-through added ~4-5 points in Q4). Q1FY27 was the fastest-growing division at +32% to ₹1,090 cr (4W wheels ₹566 cr, 2W wheels ₹284 cr, die casting ₹248 cr, +66%). Management says penetration is "inching up again" and that castings earn above the company average because they need more capital. Capacity is the story: Kharkhoda (₹542 cr, 120k 4W wheels a month: 60k running, 30k more in H2FY27), Bawal 2W (₹196 cr, ~1 mn wheels a year, HPDC, H2FY27), CSN 4W (₹792 cr, 1.8 mn wheels a year, Phase 1 Q2FY28) and EV castings at CSN (₹210 cr): ~9.5 mn 2W and ~7 mn 4W wheels a year once all are built.

Management sees ₹2,500-3,000 cr of peak revenue from ~₹1,200 cr of EV capex; new businesses reach target margins "in the third full year of production". **Seating** (₹1,416 cr, +23%) adds ~₹390 cr of peak-value export orders (Europe, North America; end-FY28 into FY29) and, after five years of trying, a passenger-car seating plant (₹320 cr, SOP Q4FY28, kit value ₹30,000-40,000 a car). **Others** (₹3,801 cr, +26%) holds sensors and ADAS (₹250 cr in Q1), acoustics (₹225 cr), blow moulding, controllers, the aftermarket and EMS; a sunroof plant (with Aisin technology) starts at end-FY27 with >₹500 cr of orders.

blocks.callout: **Verdict: a narrow moat.** Uno Minda's advantage is real but procedural: it is the easiest one-stop supplier for an Indian OEM across dozens of parts, with partners' technology behind it and a record of delivering plants on time. It is not a pricing moat (margins have never left 10.6-12.3%), and in its biggest categories it faces capable rivals. The moat shows up in growth and returns on capital, not in margins.

sections.title: Revenue up eight times in eleven years at a steady 11% margin: growth is the whole story

blocks.p: Uno Minda's revenue was ₹2,527 cr in FY16 and ₹19,658 cr in FY26: 23% a year for a decade, and 25% a year since the Covid year FY21, against Indian vehicle production that grew low-to-mid single digits a year over the same decade. The growth came from three sources: more products per vehicle (lighting, alloy wheels, seats, sensors, EV chargers), more customers and higher share with each, and acquisitions or buy-outs of partners (Harita Seating, Kosei's alloy-wheel ventures, Rinder, Clarton, FRIWO's EV stake). What did not change is the margin: EBITDA has stayed between 10.6% and 12.3% of revenue since FY17. Owners' EPS went from ₹3.8 (FY21) to ₹20.7 (FY26), 40% a year off a Covid base, and from ₹5.9 (FY18, the pre-Covid peak) at 17% a year.

Each rupee of revenue earns the same ~11 paise of EBITDA it did ten years ago; returns are good (ROE 17-19% since FY23) because assets turn ~4 times a year, not because margins are high. sections.title: Growth eats the cash: ₹6,100 cr of capex in six years, free cash flow near zero

blocks.p: Uno Minda reinvests almost everything. Over FY21-26 it generated ₹5,299 cr of operating cash, spent ₹6,129 cr on capex, ₹452 cr on acquisitions and partner buy-outs (Screener), and paid ₹524 cr of dividends (payout 12-14% of profit). Net debt (borrowings incl. leases less cash and investments, which include ₹924 cr of JV stakes at book) rose from ₹390 cr to ₹1,431 cr; on the company's definition (excluding leases and JV book value) it was ₹2,179 cr at Mar-2026, 0.30x equity. FY27 capex is guided at ₹1,750 cr, the highest ever, with ₹3,788 cr of announced projects (₹1,406 cr already spent by Jun-2026). Returns have held up: ROCE 18-20% on Screener's basis since FY23 (the company's 19.2% in FY26 includes land and CWIP not yet earning).

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit and decent cash conversion; watch incentives, one-off income and the JV line

bullets: **Cash conversion is adequate.** Cash from operations was ₹1,720 cr in FY26, 144% of owners' profit and 76% of EBITDA (57-65% in FY23-25, when working capital absorbed cash). Capex took it all.

**State incentives are in revenue.** FY26 revenue includes ₹176 cr of government grants (₹112 cr in FY25), of which ₹157 cr is industrial promotion subsidy under Maharashtra's PSI 2013 and Gujarat's 2015 policy: ~7% of EBITDA. They are earned on investment, but they are finite and accrued before cash arrives (₹175 cr receivable at Mar-26).

**One-off income in Q1FY26.** ₹69 cr of prior-period income (customer price settlements) was booked in revenue and EBITDA; the company itself reports "normalised" numbers without it. FY26 EBITDA margin: 11.5% reported, 11.1% normalised.
**Exceptional items are small.** A ₹27.6 cr labour-code charge in FY26 and small remeasurement gains in FY24-25: after tax, 1-3% of profit. We forecast none.
**The JV line is profit, but not all of it is cash.** The ₹249 cr share of JV profit compared with ₹137 cr of JV dividends received; it is 21% of owners' profit and growing.
**Related parties.** Services bought from promoter-linked entities (Paripal Advisory, Minda Investments, Minda Advisory: ~₹17 cr) and dealings with JVs are disclosed and small relative to revenue.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Unqualified audit by S.R. Batliboi & Co. (EY), modest exceptional items and positive cash conversion. The amber is for the size of state incentives inside revenue, the prior-period income that flattered FY26, and the growing share of profit that comes from JVs whose cash reaches Uno Minda only as dividends.

Working capital is lean: receivables 50 days, inventory 62 days, payables 75 days. In our model net debt peaks in FY27E (capex ₹1,750 cr) and falls from FY28E as the new plants earn.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a well-run compounder priced at 35.2x Sep-28E EPS; HOLD

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** a broad, promoter-run Indian auto-parts maker that has grown revenue ~23% a year for a decade by adding products and customers, with Japanese partners in its best JVs, 18-20% returns on capital, moderate debt and a pipeline of new plants (EV powertrain, alloy wheels, PV seats, sunroofs) that should keep revenue growing 17-19% a year to FY29E. Margins are ordinary (~11%) and will stay so: this is volume and content growth, not pricing power.

**What you are paying:** 48.2x our FY27E and 38.9x FY28E EPS for ~21% a year EPS growth. assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Uno Minda Ltd (consolidated, Rs crore). FY26 is the last reported year (revenue Rs19,658 cr incl. Rs69 cr of prior-period income). One reported segment, so revenue is a single growth path computed from the six-division build in `build` and checked in tools/authoring/UNOMINDA.ctx.js. Net profit is on the owners' basis (UNOMINDA.patch.js); the engine has no line for the share of JV profit (post-tax) or minorities, so both enter `otherIncome` grossed up for tax (see _otherIncomeWhy). Valued on P/E, as the street does; the multiple is derived in UNOMINDA.ctx.js and written here by UNOMINDA.val.js.
assumptions._revenueWhy: From the division build. FY27E +19.2% on reported FY26 (+19.6% on the Rs19,589 cr ex prior-period income): Q1FY27 grew 26% (normalised) with industry production +22%; from Q3 the base includes the GST 2.0 boost (Sep-2025), so we assume growth slows through the year. Switches +15%, Lighting +12%, Castings +22% (Kharkhoda 4W wheels, Bawal 2W wheels, aluminium pass-through), Green Mobility +60% (Q1 +78%: EV systems, 4W EDU supplies, CNG), Seating +20%, Others +17% (sensors/ADAS, sunroof from end-FY27). FY28E +17.9% and FY29E +16.9%: production +5-7% plus content, new plants (CSN wheels and EV powertrain Q2FY28, 4W seating Q4FY28) and orders already won (2W lamps Rs450 cr peak, seating exports Rs390 cr, sunroof >Rs500 cr). Street FY27E/FY28E revenue: Rs23,438-23,922 cr / Rs27,253-28,344 cr.
assumptions._marginWhy: Guidance 11% +/-50bp for FY27 'with a bias towards the higher end' (4-Aug-2026). Q1FY27 10.3% (commodity and wage inflation, ~40bp dilution from at-cost pass-through); FY26 11.1% normalised (11.5% reported incl. the prior-period income); 10.7-12.3% since FY17. FY27E 11.1% assumes ~11.3% for Q2-Q4 as price resets catch up; FY28E 11.4% and FY29E 11.5% as new plants pass their start-up year, partly offset by lower-margin EV and electronics. Street: ICICI Direct 11.1%/11.5%, Emkay 10.8%/11.5%/11.6%.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27E Rs1,750 cr guided (~Rs650 cr sustaining, ~Rs1,100 cr growth, balance land; reiterated 4-Aug-2026). Announced projects Rs3,788 cr, Rs1,406 cr spent by Jun-2026, ~Rs2,000 cr more over 18-24 months. FY26 cash capex Rs1,572 cr. FY28E Rs1,600 cr, FY29E Rs1,500 cr (sustaining ~Rs700 cr plus the tail of announced projects).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A Rs704 cr = 8.2% of average gross block (Rs8,566 cr). Part of capex is land (not depreciated) and the engine depreciates new capex at once while CWIP stays flat, so 7.8%: FY27E ~Rs800 cr (Q1FY27 Rs177 cr; Q4FY26 Rs192 cr; casting is on WDV, so Q1 is seasonally low), FY28E ~Rs930 cr, FY29E ~Rs1,050 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net debt company: Rs2,179 cr at Mar-2026 (borrowings Rs2,537 cr less cash and bank Rs358 cr; leases Rs203 cr more). Interest income is tiny (deposits Rs8 cr in FY26) and is in the recurring other income below.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built, not plugged: (1) recurring other income Rs28 / 30 / 32 cr (FY26 Rs34 cr incl. Rs5 cr tax-refund interest and Rs6 cr write-backs; Q1FY27 Rs6 cr); (2) share of JV and associate profit, post-tax, Rs270 / 310 / 350 cr (FY26 Rs249 cr, +38%; Q1FY27 Rs48 cr, flat, hit by commodity costs that the company expects to recover from Q2; Toyoda Gosei airbag plant from Q1FY27; Denso Ten IVI order Rs600 cr peak from Q3FY29) less (3) minorities Rs97 / 110 / 124 cr (FY26 Rs87 cr, Q1FY27 Rs20 cr; mostly Tokai Rika's 49% of Uno Mindarika). dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~4.6% of revenue in FY29E to 4.5% (FY22-26 average 7.7% in a heavy build phase; ~4% sustaining plus growth); depreciation 3.5% of revenue (FY26 3.6%).
dcf._jvWhy: FCFF excludes JV profit (cash comes as dividends: Rs137 cr in FY26) and includes minorities' share; JVs enter only at book value (Rs924 cr) through investments in net debt. See the DCF chapter for the effect.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Industry volumes keep growing high single digits after the GST step; EV powertrain, sunroof, PV seating and exports ramp on time; alloy-wheel penetration rises again; margin reaches the top of the 11-12% band as commodity costs ease.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Volumes flatten against the GST base; commodity and wage inflation is recovered late; new plants ramp slowly (Inovance JV blocked by Chinese approvals); share losses at a key 4W client continue; margin slips back to ~10.5%.
